answer: Let trust begin outside a sybil set \(S\) and propagate through a calibrated, bounded-length random walk. Each step can enter \(S\) only across its boundary; low conductance makes that flow small, bounding the cluster’s reachable trust—and aggregate voting weight—by cumulative boundary flow plus any initial seed mass inside \(S\). Spectral and min-cut checks reveal this bottleneck, so the kernel does not mistake dense internal links, from summit to nadir, for independent attestations.
